stop.name: Liberty Island
stop.invite: Before it was the home of the Statue of Liberty, this small island was a pest house, a fort shaped like an eleven-pointed star, and a place with a different name.
story: Liberty Island is a federally owned island in Upper New York Bay of about 14.7 acres. Wikipedia says it was originally called Bedloe's Island, and that Congress made the name Liberty Island official in 1956. Over the centuries it was a private summer estate, then a pest house bought by the City of New York in 1758, and in 1800 the New York State Legislature ceded it to the federal government for a fort.

Fort Wood, an eleven-point star fort with 24 guns, was built there between 1806 and 1811. Its granite walls later became the base on which the statue's pedestal stands. The pedestal was finished on April 22, 1886, and the statue, a gift from the people of France, was dedicated by President Grover Cleveland on October 28, 1886. The military post was fully removed by 1944. The island is now run by the National Park Service as part of the Statue of Liberty National Monument.

This card is about the island and its layers of history, not the statue itself, which already has its own stop in the New York town missions. The contributor's photo, taken in 2026, shows the statue and its pedestal beyond a flagpole and a paved plaza, with the sun high above. No old photo of the island has been added yet.

facts.t: Liberty Island covers about 14.7 acres, was originally called Bedloe's Island, and was officially renamed Liberty Island by Congress in 1956.
Fort Wood, an 11-point star fort, was built from 1806 to 1811 and its granite walls later formed the base of the Statue of Liberty.
The pedestal was finished on April 22, 1886 and the statue was dedicated on October 28, 1886.
Statue City Cruises is the only authorized ferry service to the island, leaving from Liberty State Park or The Battery, and visitors pass airport-style security before boarding.
Pedestal and crown access require advance purchase; the crown climb is 162 steps with no elevator.

stop.access: Liberty Island can only be reached by the Statue City Cruises ferry from Liberty State Park or The Battery, after airport-style security. Check the National Park Service page for current tickets and hours before you go.
